Thanks, Nadia — that's a critical finding. The location data in activity payloads changes the picture significantly. Tokenization before entering the bus and EU-region storage both sound like hard requirements for privacy sign-off, and they directly conflict with two elements of the current draft RFC (unrestricted payload publishing and default US region storage). I'm noting that as a must-address before approval.

Maya, before we get to your compatibility issue, let me make sure I have the privacy constraints straight: we need tokenization applied before events hit the bus, and storage must be EU region. Are there any additional privacy requirements beyond those two, or is that the full scope of what needs to change?

And Maya, please go ahead and walk us through your compatibility finding after that — I want to make sure we capture all the blockers before we discuss revisions.

transcript.text: While tracing an unrelated SDK issue yesterday, I confirmed that three named legacy consumers can only read the current Avro envelope. This means the migration needs an Avro compatibility gateway and exactly 21 days of dual publishing. I haven't updated the RFC yet to reflect this, but it's a hard constraint — without the gateway and the dual-publishing period, those consumers will break when we move to the new event bus.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have replay benchmark results from this morning that are relevant to the RFC. The benchmark showed that the expected peak backlog can be recovered safely with at most 4 concurrent replay workers and exactly 14 days of retained events. The 14-day retention result is independent of Maya's dual-publishing period. I haven't posted the benchmark yet because I'm still checking the dashboard screenshots, but I wanted to share these findings now since we're discussing retention and replay constraints.
